one_liner: Hand-rolled NEON SIMD lexer for a toy language; beats the Rust logos crate 20-35% on Apple M1.
what_it_does: lnpl is the lexer for a personal toy-language compiler project (crate name "lnpl"), tokenizing source into its own Token/TokenKind enum for the author's Pratt-parser front end. It is not a general-purpose lexer generator: there's no derive-macro or grammar-spec input like logos has, so using it means adapting its hardcoded token set, not swapping in your own grammar. On non-aarch64 targets the crate falls back to a separate, unbenchmarked generic::Lexer implementation.
how_it_is_fast: The aarch64 path loads input in 512-byte chunks into an aligned SIMD buffer and uses NEON 128-bit vector loads to classify 16 ASCII bytes at once (ident/whitespace/number/etc. character classes), with hand-written NEON assembly (aarch64.s) pulled in via global_asm!. Keyword matching uses a perfect hash that packs each keyword into a 64-bit word for single-instruction comparison instead of a DFA/trie walk. The author also reports a 5-10% gain from replacing a computed classification mask with a precomputed lookup table.
when_to_use: You're targeting aarch64 (Apple Silicon or ARM servers) specifically -- there is no x86_64 SIMD path
You want a worked example of NEON-based ASCII token classification plus perfect-hash keyword matching to adapt into your own lexer
Your token stream is dominated by short, repetitive keyword/identifier patterns, where the gain over logos is largest (~35% on the synthetic benchmark)
You can build with an unpinned Rust nightly and are comfortable vendoring unsafe/asm source rather than depending on a published crate
Throughput on medium files (5KB-1MB) matters more than lexer generality or ergonomics
when_not_to_use: x86_64 targets: the author's own numbers show the naive scalar lexer beating logos there, and no NEON-equivalent path exists
You need a drop-in replacement for logos's `#[derive(Logos)]` API -- lnpl's token types are hardcoded to the author's toy language
You need stable Rust: the crate uses `#![feature(core_intrinsics)]` and `#![feature(stdsimd)]`, unstable nightly-only features
You need a maintained dependency: no crates.io release found, last commit April 2024, no README, and it's explicitly experimental research code
Your workload looks like realistic, non-repetitive source rather than synthetic pseudocode -- the measured gain shrinks from ~35% to ~20% on the real Hubris kernel snippets

integration.dependencies: logos 0.13 (used only for parity testing / bench comparison, not by the aarch64 lexer itself)
integration.min_toolchain: Rust nightly (unpinned; requires core_intrinsics + stdsimd unstable features; .cargo/config.toml sets rustflags = -Zpolonius)
integration.platforms: aarch64 (NEON) for the benchmarked/optimized path; a generic fallback exists for other architectures but is not benchmarked or discussed
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial -- different Token/TokenKind API from logos's derive-macro model; you'd port token definitions, not swap a dependency

gotchas: Contains raw NEON assembly (aarch64.s) loaded via global_asm! plus unsafe SIMD intrinsics -- review before vendoring
Uses a fixed 512-byte, 128-byte-aligned SIMD input buffer (SimdBuffer); behavior at buffer boundaries wasn't verified in this review
Depends on nightly-only, unstable compiler features (core_intrinsics, stdsimd) with no pinned rustc version

The published benchmark numbers on the blog labeled the lnpl result 'logos:' (apparent typo) -- read the repo's bench source (benches/lexer.rs), not just the blog table, to confirm which number is which
pick_this_over_siblings_when: None of the catalogued siblings target Rust + logos on aarch64, so this is the only entry showing that specific pairing; pick it only as a technique reference for NEON ASCII classification + perfect-hash keywords, not as an installable lexer -- for an actual drop-in tokenizer, Accelerated-Zig-Parser or simd-lexing are more complete SIMD lexers, and logos itself (already catalogued) remains the safer general-purpose choice off aarch64.
verified_claims_summary: First-party `cargo bench` results (unpinned Rust nightly, single Apple M1 machine) show lnpl's NEON lexer at 118,476 ns/iter vs logos 0.13 at 174,476 ns/iter tokenizing a 100KB synthetic pseudocode file (~35% faster), and 89,151 ns/iter vs logos's 108,257 ns/iter (~1.21x) on real Hubris-kernel source snippets (5KB-1MB); the author separately reports 20-30% gains across that Hubris file-size range.
status_note: Stale since April 2024 with zero open issues and no crates.io listing found; MPL-2.0 licensed research code from a personal toy-compiler project, small enough to vendor the lexer module but not maintained or packaged as a library.
